item.title: Newscast: Tuesday, Oct. 27, 2026
item.description: In this newscast: Goldbelt Incorporated is a step closer toward its plan to build a $500 million cruise ship port in Juneau. The State of Alaska issued a preliminary decision last week to approve a 25-year lease of state-owned tidelands on Douglas Island to the Alaska Native corporation; The Juneau Assembly bid farewell to two longtime members at its meeting Monday night and unanimously voted to reject an ordinance to establish regulations for electric motorcycle use in city parks, trails, and recreation areas and on designated Eaglecrest trails. Assembly members plan to pursue a different ordinance that would enact citywide regulations; Data centers are proliferating in rural areas across the United States to support the rapidly developing artificial intelligence (AI) industry. And proposals to construct them in Southeast Alaska have recently cropped up in Wrangell and Petersburg. At a meeting on Wednesday, the Sitka Planning Commission recommended prohibiting the construction of data centers, at least for now; Ketchikan’s city council last winter approved updates to its municipal code that limit where people can sit, lie or camp within city limits. The changes were met with both support and opposition, with some arguing that they could negatively impact the city’s unhoused population.

item.title: Newscast – Monday, Oct. 26, 2026
item.description: In this newscast: The Juneau School Board will consider a complaint over curriculum being used at Kax̲dig̲oowu Héen Elementary at its Tuesday meeting; Both candidates vying for the open House District 3 seat in the Alaska Legislature say they aren't convinced the state's controversial Cascade Point ferry terminal project will benefit Southeast communitites; The monthlong moose hunt near Petersburg, Wrangell and Kake closed in mid-October, and final harvest numbers show it was another record-breaking season; The U.S. Senate campaign of Democrat Mary Peltola is among those asking a federal judge to dismiss a Department of Justice lawsuit that could block or delay election results if she wins; A high school student from Angoon speaks on her award-winning short film about the U.S. Navy's bombardment of the village 144 years ago.
